title: Full-Stack Modern React and Next.js Application Development
description: Twenty original draft lessons with executable dependency-free JavaScript checkpoints and bounded interactive scenario labs. The pathway covers React, Node/document data, APIs, identity, rendering, testing, analytics, GraphQL, realtime, Next.js, caching, and a private notebook capstone. Framework builds and deployment remain learner project work.
prerequisites: Use an editor and navigate a folder
learningOutcomes: Build and test a private note workflow across UI, API, and owner-scoped storage
Model asynchronous data, GraphQL mutations, and realtime replay with explicit failure states
Choose React and Next.js boundaries, metadata, and caching policies
Validate inputs, authorization, privacy, accessibility, and release gates with evidence
accessibilityNotes: All essential content is text with static diagrams
Optional decorative GIFs are collapsed and play once for 2.4 seconds; GitHub cannot apply OS reduced-motion settings to GIFs
No animation, precise location, or public profile is required
Framework exercises require keyboard and mobile review

chapters.title: Foundations: make one observable change
chapters.summary: Orientation, environment checks, browser/server distinctions, and the first component learning loop.
objectives: Describe browser, server, and file responsibilities
Run and change a JavaScript checkpoint
Connect a heading to a component
prerequisites: Recognize an HTML heading and a JavaScript string

chapters.title: JavaScript data and TypeScript contracts
chapters.summary: Immutable transformations, static types, and runtime checks with meaningful edge cases.

chapters.title: React: describe the next interface
chapters.summary: Props, state, transitions, events, and a labeled form practice extension.
objectives: Separate input, state, event, and output
Connect a labeled control to UI changes

chapters.title: Node.js and document data
chapters.summary: Model asynchronous server work, owner-scoped document queries, projection, and storage lifetimes.
objectives: Distinguish asynchronous I/O from synchronous computation
Filter and project a synthetic document collection

chapters.title: APIs: make a small HTTP contract
chapters.summary: Validate a note creation endpoint and test status codes without opening a network port.
objectives: Map method and path to a request contract
Test successful and unsuccessful HTTP outcomes

chapters.title: Asynchronous data and request races
chapters.summary: Keep server-state cache identity, out-of-order responses, retries, and refresh failures understandable.
objectives: Represent loading, empty, success, and error states

chapters.title: Data, validation, persistence, and identity
chapters.summary: Validate before writes, scope ownership to trusted identity, and state storage guarantees honestly.

chapters.title: Identity, sessions, and access
chapters.summary: Trace trusted identity into authorization and reason about cookies, expiry, and forged requests.
objectives: Check ownership and expiry at the server boundary
Describe session and token exposure risks

chapters.title: Rendering and meaningful discovery
chapters.summary: Compare server and client rendering, useful initial HTML, metadata, canonical URLs, and private routes.
objectives: Inspect initial HTML separately from hydrated UI
Choose public metadata and canonical origin
Keep private pages protected and out of indexing

chapters.title: Quality: prove behavior and include people
chapters.summary: Behavior tests, keyboard and form review, safe URL policies, and the limits of automated evidence.
objectives: Review labels, focus, and keyboard use

chapters.title: Learning insights without surveillance
chapters.summary: Aggregate minimal consented events, deduplicate delivery, and explain small-group suppression.
objectives: Label chart limits and data freshness

chapters.title: GraphQL: a bounded server contract
chapters.summary: Select public fields, validate query depth, and authorize each synthetic resolver.
objectives: Describe fields, variables, queries, and mutations
Apply authorization independently of query shape

chapters.title: GraphQL: client state and mutations
chapters.summary: Model normalized identity, optimistic updates, duplicate confirmations, and targeted rollback.
objectives: Reconcile a confirmed mutation without duplication

chapters.title: Realtime: authenticated server events
chapters.summary: Check connection identity, room membership, payload limits, storage failure, and acknowledgement order.

chapters.title: Realtime: reconnect and reconcile
chapters.summary: Bound offline queues, preserve client IDs across retries, and deduplicate confirmations.
objectives: Represent connected, pending, offline, and failed states

chapters.title: Realtime: durable replay and retention
chapters.summary: Combine scoped idempotency, sequence cursors, owner filtering, and retention in an event log.
objectives: Replay after a stable sequence cursor
Apply owner and retention limits to reads

chapters.title: Next.js: routes and execution boundaries
chapters.summary: App Router routes and layouts, safe server/client props, and explicit data states.

chapters.title: Caching, invalidation, and performance
chapters.summary: Partition private caches, invalidate after writes, and enforce a useful asset budget.
objectives: Choose cache identity and shared-cache policy
Reproduce and fix a stale read
Measure a budget without inventing performance claims

chapters.title: Git, CI, deployment concepts, and recovery
chapters.summary: Local diff review, reproducible checks, least privilege, release approval, and rollback rehearsal.
objectives: Review a local change before staging

chapters.title: Capstone: a private learning notebook
chapters.summary: A bounded local app brief combining routes, forms, validated persistence, tests, accessibility, and a retrospective.
objectives: Build a complete local note workflow

completion.rule: Complete all twenty server-checked scenario activities and practice the authored checkpoints; record project tests and reflections. Scenario passing verifies the bounded model only, not framework mastery, production readiness, or a credential. Review capstone implementation evidence separately.
